hero.caption: Prefontaine Building, 110 Prefontaine Place South, Pioneer Square neighborhood, Seattle, Washington, USA. Built 1909. This building is named for Father Francis X. Prefontaine, a French Canadian priest who had built Seattle's first Catholic church on this site. Father Prefontaine died in 1909, the same year that this building was constructed.

images.caption: Father Francis Xavier Prefontaine and the Our Lady of Good Help Church in Seattle, Washington. The church was built by Father Prefontaine beginning in 1869, and became the first Catholic Church in Seattle. By 1882, the church had become too small to accommodate the nearly 300 parishioners. Fr. Prefontaine remodeled the church, which continued to serve as a central base for the priests traveling to missions in the Puget Sound area. In 1905 the church was demolished and rebuilt on a new site. Fr. Prefontaine died in 1909.
